svg.text: Human Skills Training - as of Nov 10, 2026 - one engine, one rulebook, one master list, two machines, three scheduled tasks
0 - THE SETUP: who we are looking for, and which machine looks for them
A CLUSTER is one Market + one Message + one Method (the TLBS three-circles model).
Many ICP files add up to one Market; a Market is one third of a cluster.
A machine = one settings block + one email template.
Same engine, same Rulebook, same master list. No new code.
1 - THE NIGHT RUN - Sun-Thu 8:41 PM, a scheduled task on Chris's Mac - makes drafts and lists, NEVER sends
One program prints the one next step; the run does it, saves a checkpoint, asks again. A crashed run resumes where it stopped.
THE MASTER LIST (one row per organization, both machines) is read by every phase and rebuilt after every phase. Gmail is the truth.
Reads every outreach thread in Gmail in full: what was sent, who replied, what bounced, which
auto-replies name a successor ('I've left - contact Jane'). Writes down the true state of every thread.
reads: Gmail, yesterday's master list -> writes: the thread-state ledger, the master list rebuilt from
Three housekeeping jobs. (a) Stray Email 1 drafts with no label: rewrite, hand to the other
machine, or delete - never left for Chris. (b) Put one label on every thread: /0 drafted, /1 /2 /3 sent,
star replied, x closed, warning needs Chris, pause hold. (c) Threads Chris must see first get their
next email saved as a DRAFT reply, never sent.
reads: Gmail drafts, the thread states, the label rules -> writes: labels and draft replies in Gmail, the
PHASE 7 (night half) - TOMORROW'S APPROVED SEND LIST
For every open thread: is Email 2 or 3 due? 7 days after the last send, business days only, delayed
past weekends and holidays, never skipped. Stopped by any reply, stop label, open draft or bounce.
Every row must pass every Rulebook check. Anything flagged is NOT approved. Final once written.
reads: the master list, the 'every address ever contacted' ledger, the calendar -> writes: the approved
THE LOOP - Discover -> Qualify -> People -> Draft, pass after pass, until each machine has its drafts
Only for machines still under their minimum. No clock. A pass that adds nothing for a machine = out of supply tonight. Runaway guard: 25 passes.
Find organizations and events we do not know yet. The program picks the sources that are due
(directories, conference calendars, keynote speakers' pages, partner pages) and gives each AI helper
a batch with an exact search allowance. Helpers read the web in parallel and follow each find outward.
The program checks every result before it counts.
reads: the places-to-look list, the search log (no search is ever repeated), ICP files -> writes: new
FIT: a quote found on the org's own live page must pass its ICP test (doubtful = draft but flag).
ROUTE: runs its own conference with an outside keynote -> OM-2; everything else -> OM-1.
TIME (OM-2): outreach opens 6 months before the event; silent inside 3 months; too close -> next year.
reads: every unjudged org, its live pages, the exclusions (do-not-contact, existing clients, Colorado) ->
Find up to 4 people per org (1 To + 3 Cc), chosen by ROLE. An address counts only if it is printed
on the org's own page or auto-reply - OR a named person with no published address is looked up in
Apollo and counts only if Apollo says Verified AND ZeroBounce says valid AND it is on the org's own
domain. A general inbox is the To only after that lookup found nobody. Zero guesses, ever.
reads: fit orgs with no thread yet, their staff pages, their auto-replies, Apollo -> writes: each org's
recipients + greeting, or why it is held
The program fills the frozen template word for word; only the greeting and the org's short name
change. Zapier creates the Gmail draft with the PDF attached. A final check reads the raw draft back
(attachment, links, Bcc, recipients, subject) before it counts. Never sent by a machine.
reads: orgs with a ready recipient set, Gmail checked first (one thread per org), the template + PDF ->
writes: Email 1 DRAFTS in Gmail, the drafts ledger
or out of organizations for tonight?
1. The SENDING DOSSIER: one card per Email 1 draft (the org, its pages, every recipient with its source,
the reasoning) - built only from the records, nothing looked up. Chris reads it beside Gmail Drafts.
2. The ONE MORNING REPORT: executive summary, then one prioritized issues list with a fix for each.
reads: the master list, the night's step log, open questions for Chris, Apollo credits -> writes: the
dossier, the report, new questions in the rulings log
1b - THE SUPPLY RUN - every day ~1 AM MT, a second scheduled task - stocks the shelf; NEVER drafts, NEVER touches Gmail
SUPPLY RUN - DISCOVER > QUALIFY > EVENTS > PEOPLE
The same four research steps as the loop, run on their own clock so the night run never starts hungry:
find new organizations, judge their fit and owner, check their events, find and verify their people - up to
this run's caps, hard stop 4:30 AM. One run at a time: it yields if a night run is alive. Its only output is
a longer, better-stocked master list; drafting stays the night run's job, sending the 7 AM task's.
reads: the places-to-look list, the master list, the org's live pages, Apollo -> writes: new rows, fit,
owner, window, recipients on the master list + a shelf table in the morning report
2 - THE MORNING - Mon-Fri - the only sending in the whole system happens here
report + dossier + approved list + a stocked list
A SEPARATE scheduled task: fires 6:52 AM ET, waits until 7:00, then sends Emails 2 and 3 - only the
rows on the approved list, exactly as listed, each thread re-read live first (a read older than 3 minutes
is stale). Anything that changed overnight is skipped and left for tonight's run to decide again.
Bounce rate over 3% stops everything. The only task allowed to act without asking.
reads: today's FINAL approved list, each thread live in Gmail, the templates, its own past sends (a
duplicate = full stop) -> writes: sent emails + moved labels in Gmail, the send record
- adds the GIF and SENDS Email 1 by hand (a machine never does)
- writes back to every real reply
- rules on flags and open questions
- changes a rule only by editing the Rulebook; a number only in the settings file
reads: the morning report, the dossier beside Gmail Drafts, replies and flags -> writes: Email 1 sent,
replies, rulings (tonight's run reads them all)
THE CYCLE (dashed line): what Chris sends and what people reply lands in Gmail. Tonight's run reads Gmail first,
so every morning's actions are in the records by the next night. Nothing is re-done: the ledgers remember.
3 - THE EMAIL SEQUENCE - same for every machine, one thread per organization, 7 days apart
written by the machine, sent by
Chris by hand with the GIF + PDF
never started again by a machine
Any real reply stops the sequence and goes to Chris - an auto-reply is never a reply - a bounce stops the thread - weekend or US holiday = delayed to the next business day, never skipped
8. Doesn't add up? Stop and hold
template filling, safety gates, 'the one next step'.
AI HELPERS (judgment): read web pages, judge fit,
find people, sort replies, write the plain-English report.
The AI never writes email copy, never picks who
gets emailed, and never sends anything.
CHARTER - why it exists, what it must never become
RULEBOOK - the rules; changes only from Chris
SETTINGS FILE - every number, one block per machine
RULINGS LOG - questions for Chris, his answers
CAPA LOG - what went wrong, the fix, the prevention
If a change does not trace to one of these, it is drift.
